messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: repeated memory OOMs observed on hosted-rt-04 and hosted-rt-07 (kv-cache growth). Alert: https://pager.redwood.example/alerts/8112

maya (oncall-sre): on it, pulling logs and heap profiles now. seeing steady kv_cache size growth tied to very long prompts.

maya (oncall-sre): quick snapshot from logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:33Z] tok=abcdef req=org-773b prompt_len=120k kv_entries=324MB total_kv=3.1GB OOM
```

jon (runtime-eng): did we roll an increased batch window yesterday? I pushed batch-window=1.5s for better throughput.

maya (oncall-sre): yeah that rollout landed across hosted pools. heap profiles show entries pinned longer because continuous batching holds prefixes and KV states. eviction not keeping up.

priya (infra): which nodes are failing?

maya (oncall-sre): hosted-rt-04 and hosted-rt-07 mostly. OOMs correlate with repeated long-streamed prompts from a few orgs.

jon (runtime-eng): plan: immediate rollback of batch window to 300ms and re-enable early KV eviction. also consider a per-request KV cap as an emergency guard.

jon (runtime-eng): commands I will run shortly:
```
# revert config
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/hosted-runtime BATCH_WINDOW_MS=300
# re-enable eviction
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/hosted-runtime KV_EVICTION_ENABLED=true
```

maya (oncall-sre): applying now. starting controlled rollout. ops-bot will track.

ops-bot: deploy started by maya (hosted-runtime config revert).

maya (oncall-sre): rolled batch-window to 300ms on hosted-* pools. watching memory.

tasha (support): which customers do I notify? any user-facing impact details?

maya (oncall-sre): affected tenants observed in logs: org-773b (chat partner), org-1234 (research provider), org-8812 (integration partner). Symptoms: intermittent 5xx generation errors and spikes in latency for requests with huge contexts.

maya (oncall-sre): rough numbers: ~0.4% of requests by count but they consume ~6-8% of KV memory due to extremely long prompts.

jon (runtime-eng): applying emergency guard: set per-request KV bytes cap to 256MB. patching control plane now.

jon (runtime-eng): curl to patch control plane config:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/configs/hosted-runtime -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"kv_per_request_limit":268435456}'
```

ops-bot: config update applied. metric kv_per_req_rejected incrementing (12 in last 30s).

maya (oncall-sre): starting rolling restarts on affected pods to drop stuck KV allocations.

priya (infra): restarting hosted-rt-07 -> restart complete. hosted-rt-04 -> restart queued.

ops-bot: hosted-rt-07 restart finished. hosted-rt-04 restart finished.

maya (oncall-sre): memory trending down on restarted nodes, no new OOMs in the last 3m.

jon (runtime-eng): followups we should do immediately:
- add a telemetry alert for kv_total_bytes per-pool
- add per-tenant KV caps and soft throttles
- add automated rollback gates for batch-window rollouts

maya (oncall-sre): customer impact note for CS: prepare a short message for org-773b and org-1234: brief outage with 5xx/errors for long-context generation. mitigations applied (config revert, per-request caps). recommend retrying with smaller context or split prompts.

tasha (support): drafting messages and queued for send. offering to pull logs for customers who request.

dylan (product): root cause summary for postmortem?

maya (oncall-sre): root cause: interaction between a recent increase to batch-window (1.5s) and heavy long-context streaming from a few tenants -> continuous batching pinned large KV prefixes longer than eviction logic expected -> KV cache growth -> OOMs.

maya (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations: revert batch-window to 300ms, re-enable eviction, apply per-request KV byte cap (256MB), restart affected pods.

priya (infra): ops note: reclaimed memory on 6 pods, system latencies returning to SLO ranges.

jon (runtime-eng): moving forward items: CI regression sim simulating streaming long prompts, add auto-evict when kv_total_bytes > threshold, add tenant throttles, and a canary rollout policy for batch window increases.

maya (oncall-sre): creating incident postmortem doc and linking telemetry graphs. assigning follow-ups to @jon and @priya.

ops-bot: incident severity set to S2, mitigation in progress.

maya (oncall-sre): leaving final handoff to next oncall: follow up on dashboards for 24h, confirm no regression spikes after full traffic return.

jon (runtime-eng): I will own the follow-ups, will open PRs for the caps + eviction change and the rollout safety checks.

maya (oncall-sre): :white_check_mark: marking pager addressed in channel. continuing post-incident work outside this thread.
